topic: Law change: ESIC fixes funeral expenses at Rs 20,000 for the death of an insured worker - Section 32(1)(f), Code on Social Security, 2020 (ESIC notification N-12011/1/2023-P&D dated 7 Oct 2026, Gazette 16 Oct 2026, effective from 8 May 2026)

slides.title: ESIC funeral help is now **Rs 20,000**
slides.subtitle: If a worker insured under ESIC dies, the family can claim **₹20,000** towards funeral costs.
slides.cite: **ESIC notification** dated 7 Oct 2026 · Section 32(1)(f), **Code on Social Security, 2020**

slides.label: What changed
slides.title: A fixed amount under the **new Code**
bullets: ESIC has fixed the funeral benefit at **₹20,000** under the Code on Social Security, 2020.
Under the old ESI framework it was **up to ₹15,000**, so this is ₹5,000 more.
Notified on **7 October 2026**, published in the Gazette on **16 October 2026**.
slides.note: **Law fact:** It applies **from 8 May 2026**, earlier than the date it was notified.

slides.label: Who can claim
slides.title: Family first, then the **one who paid**
bullets: The **eldest surviving family member** of the deceased insured person.
If the worker had **no family**, or was **not living with family** at the time of death, the person who **actually paid** for the funeral.
It is meant to help with **funeral costs**. It is not a pension or compensation.

slides.label: How to claim
slides.title: Go to the **ESIC Branch Office**
bullets: Use ESIC's funeral expenses claim form (**Form 22**) and submit it at the ESIC Branch Office.
Keep ready: **death certificate**, the deceased's **ESIC insurance number**, and your own details and proof of entitlement.
The old rule allowed **3 months** from death. The new notice sets no separate limit, so **apply early**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Only for **ESIC-insured** workers
bullets: This is **not** a payment for every death. The deceased must be an **insured person** under ESIC, as per its records.
ESI contribution rates for workers and employers have **not** changed. The employer does not pay this ₹20,000 directly.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

lines: One important legal update every day, in simple words.

caption:
ESIC now gives ₹20,000 towards the funeral of an insured worker 🕯️⚖️

The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has fixed the funeral benefit at ₹20,000 under Section 32(1)(f) of the Code on Social Security, 2020. Under the old ESI framework the amount was up to ₹15,000. The notification is dated 7 October 2026, was published in the Gazette on 16 October 2026, and applies from 8 May 2026.

Who can claim? The eldest surviving member of the family of the deceased insured person. If the worker had no family, or was not living with the family at the time of death, the person who actually paid for the funeral can claim it. The claim is made on ESIC's Form 22 at the ESIC Branch Office, with the death certificate, the deceased's ESIC insurance number and the claimant's details.

The old rule gave 3 months from the date of death to claim. The new notification does not set a separate time limit, so it is safest to apply early. Remember, this benefit is only for persons insured under ESIC. It does not change ESI contribution rates, and the employer does not have to pay this amount directly.

Law: Section 32(1)(f), Code on Social Security, 2020, read with Rule 21, Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 | ESIC Notification No. N-12011/1/2023-P&D dated 7 October 2026
